speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; how long do these episodes typically last, and do you or anyone else witness jerking movements or loss of bladder control during them?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Epilepsy with automatisms (likely Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy variant given the hand gestures and post-ictal state, or focal impaired awareness seizures evolving from frontal lobe). The muddy taste (gustatory aura) and hand gestures suggest a focal onset, but the staring and unresponsiveness mimic absence. REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram) with hyperventilation and photic stimulation. REQUEST IMAGES: None required at this stage; EEG is critical for confirmation.
